label: round 8, phase F — the strip was never in the inset
notes: Wil's three asks, answered against phase A2's measured geometry rather than re-derived. THE GEOMETRY (his phone, at rest, Top layout): the top bar covers screen y 0-107 which is document offsets -107 to 0; the visible page is y 107-752 = offsets 0-645; the bottom toolbar covers y 752-844 = offsets 645-737. In-flow content is NOT clipped, so real content renders behind the BOTTOM bar; a pinned box IS clipped at the visual viewport (A2: 160px of requested bleed, 21px rendered). ASK 2 SHIPPED. Phase C's strip failed because it was at top:0, which the geometry puts at screen y 107 -- BELOW the address bar, in visible page area. It was never in the region it was meant to fill, so the four-commit opacity sweep was measuring the wrong thing. Parked at top:-12px it is inside the obscured inset where the same clip that blocks the corridor makes it unpaintable, while still qualifying as a sampler (the brief and the community suite both record off-screen-past-the-edge as read). Safari then paints its opaque background extension across the whole top inset -- Safari's own UI fill, not page paint, which is why scrolling cannot composite content over it and the body fallback never could. Opaque #100a06, static. ALSO FIXED, and it was a real defect: Base.astro's sampler set an INLINE background-color on .edge-glass-top from the section under the top edge, and an inline style beats the stylesheet, so the element meant to hold one colour was repainted per section on every scroll frame. That write is removed; `best = sc` stays for the theme-color meta (Chrome for Android, phase C4). ASK 1 -- /map's top bar at rest is PHYSICALLY IMPOSSIBLE, measured twice independently: the region is document offsets -107 to 0 and there is no document there. It is not a tint problem. The moment the reader scrolls the bars minimize and 'nothing is covered' (A2), so the top bar already shows the map exactly as the bottom does; the matched #353535 is the ceiling for the at-rest state only. No code change, and it should not be chased again. ASK 3 -- /paintings' bottom cannot show the corridor: the stage is position:sticky and its paint is clipped at the visual viewport, so canvas pixels cannot reach offsets 645-737 however tall the box is. AND the band is ALREADY the corridor's own colour -- the three.js scene background is #1d1411, identical to the page ground now showing there -- so a matched fill would change nothing visible. The only remaining fix is taking the corridor out of sticky, which is that page's scroll mechanic; not attempted under 'do not break anything', raised for Wil's decision. allowedRoutes stays empty: the strip must be a no-op on every route at every breakpoint. NOTE: qa:snap captures the viewport at scroll 0 and therefore cannot photograph an off-screen strip either way; the no-paint claim rests on A2's measured clip plus the certainty that a fixed box at top:-12px is outside the viewport wherever there are no bars.
